title: Half the world in one circle
hook: More people live inside this circle than outside it.
notes: Circle after Danny Quah (2015), refining a 2013 observation by Reddit user valeriepieris: radius ≈ 3,300 km, centred near Mong Khet, Myanmar. Population figures ≈ 2025, UN World Population Prospects 2024, rounded.

scenes.title: Draw a circle here
scenes.text: Centre it in northern Myanmar and give it a radius of about 3,300 km. Inside: India, Bangladesh, most of China and Pakistan, and nearly all of Southeast Asia. More than half of all humans. Japan is just outside.

scenes.title: Where people actually are
scenes.text: Population by country. Two countries, India and China, have about 1.4 billion people each. Together they hold more than a third of the world.

scenes.title: The empty side
scenes.text: Turn the globe around and you find a hemisphere that is almost entirely water. Fewer than one in twenty people live on this side of the planet.

scenes.title: Population on the globe
scenes.text: The same numbers on a sphere. Africa is the fastest-growing region: Nigeria alone has about 240 million people today.
